title: How do I put an @ sign in the help file of a plugin?

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
My URL contains an @ sign but it breaks the help file as soon as the engine reads it.
This will be a free plugin for the community btw
Edit:
Now available!

posts.author: Trihan
posts.body: It doesn't appear that you can. The symbol itself causes the parser to think you've started a directive line. Unicode and HTML codes don't seem to work.

posts.author: OcRam
posts.body:
Some might use "Fullwidth" (U+FF20) ＠ or "Small" (U+FE6
﹫ at characters for that. But that requires plugin to be in UTF-8 format.
Since that normal U+0040 @ COMMERCIAL AT is indeed reserved.
Edit: that sunglass ment to be ... U+FE6B

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
The problem with using a look-alike is that
youtube.com/＠AquaEchoGames
is no longer a valid URL (leading to Youtube's 404 page), which kind of defeats the point of a link.
I've tried a bunch of different ways to hopefully make the parser ignore a
@
, but none of them worked. Amusingly, if can add
@help
in the middle of a help file it will discard the previous one and restart from here.
It's interesting that you seem to be the first person to run into this problem, I'd expect something like this to crop up a lot faster than so many years after introducing the system.
